Gmnotes: Script: Use the prompt bank and Connection Builder. Ask each player for at least one connection in quick mode. Save accepted, clarified, complicated, or passed results. Process: character postcards, one anchor connection, one tension/trust connection, then one group memory. Show players only the active prompt and permission language, not the whole GM prompt bank. Checklist: At least one connection target per player; Connection Builder entries saved; Group memory asked if time allows; Ask one optional world-connection question per player if the table has energy.; Log answers as table-contributed canon when they point at a faction, NPC, or location.
Gmscript: Use the prompt bank and Connection Builder. Ask each player for at least one connection in quick mode. Save accepted, clarified, complicated, or passed results.

Gmreadaloud: Connections are quick relationship prompts. One player offers a memory or relationship question, and another player answers from their character's point of view. You are not writing someone else's character. You are offering a hook. The other player can accept it, clarify it, complicate it, soften it, or pass. We only need enough connection to make the party feel like people who can start the job together.

Gmchecklist: At least one connection target per player Connection Builder entries saved Group memory asked if time allows Ask one optional world-connection question per player if the table has energy. Log answers as table-contributed canon when they point at a faction, NPC, or location.

Gmexamples: World connection example: "Somebody you knew got buried in debt. Who were they, and who held the note?" The answer becomes table canon and can attach to Goldwater, Soulspire, or another fitting faction. World connection example: "What slogan have you heard too many times?" Use the player's answer to make the next faction feel like it has already touched their life. Rules-backed pattern: one player offers a first-person shared-history prompt, another player answers from their character's memory, and anyone can turn down a bad fit. Module example: Marlowe can use 'I owe you a favor.' Ask another PC what happened, then let them accept, clarify, complicate, soften, or pass. P2P example: 'We've run a delivery that went wrong before. What did we agree never to tell anyone?' Keep the answer short enough to play tonight.
Playertakeaway: Players can create connections by offering, accepting, clarifying, complicating, softening, or passing.
Storytakeaway: The PCs enter the job with at least one relationship already alive.
Mechanictakeaway: Uses Daggerheart-style connection prompts to build party relationships before play.

If someone asks what to say: "Try: which PC saw you choose a person over a policy, or which PC knows why you really accepted this contract?" Playerquestions: There is a company everyone in the territories deals with that you personally do not trust. What is it to you, and what did it cost you? You have carried freight before. Tell me about the one parcel you wish you had never agreed to move. Somebody you knew got buried in debt they could not climb out of. Who were they to you, and who held the note? What slogan have you heard so many times you can recite it in your sleep, and how do you feel when you hear it now? You have met one of the undead laborers up close. What did that encounter leave you believing? Name a place out here that felt wrong the moment you stepped into it. What was off? Who taught you not to trust the people in nice livery? What happened to them? What small kindness did a stranger do for you on the road that you have never forgotten?
